events.summary: Under the statutes of the Banque Centrale des Comores, signed in Paris on 22 April 2008 and still in force, the bank's board has at most eight members, half of them designated by the French Government and half by the Government of the Union of the Comoros, so every seat is filled by one of the two governments. The Governor is named by the President of the Union of the Comoros, on a proposal from the Minister of Finance. This is a standing arrangement with no end date; the bank's board approved a new draft of the statutes on 28 June 2024, but that text still awaited promulgation by the Union's President at the end of 2024.

events.summary: President Mahmoud Abbas issued a presidential decree reconstituting the board of directors of the Palestine Monetary Authority, acting on a recommendation from the Cabinet and from the Authority's Governor. Three of the eight seats are held by virtue of law: the Governor as chairman, the Deputy Governor, and a representative of the Ministry of Finance, named as Majdi Al-Hassan. The report does not name the law that gives those seats.

events.summary: Macao's Chief Executive, Sam Hou Fai, appointed Vong Sin Man, a worker of the Statistics and Census Service, as a member of the board of directors of the Monetary Authority of Macao, from 1 July to 31 December 2025. The order is made under article 50 of the Basic Law and articles 4(2)(a), 14 and 15(1) and (2) of the Monetary Authority's Statute, approved by Decree-Law 14/96/M of 11 March 1996, which the order shows is still the law in force: under that statute the head of the executive appoints the Authority's board. The pay for the post is borne by the Monetary Authority. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.

events.summary: The Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan 2010, passed by Parliament on 2 June 2010 and in force from 22 June 2010, lets the executive direct the central bank: section 149 says the Royal Government may from time to time issue directives to the Authority, after consulting the Governor, and must report them to Parliament. Of the Board's seven members, four are appointed by the Government and one of those must come from the Ministry of Finance; the Governor is appointed, and may be removed, by the Druk Gyalpo on the Prime Minister's recommendation, and the Royal Government sets the Governor's salary and the board members' fees. The Act repealed the 1982 Royal Monetary Authority Act. This is a standing arrangement with no end date.
events.source_title: The Royal Monetary Authority Act of Bhutan 2010 (Parliament of Bhutan)

events.summary: Under the statutes set by law no. 118/AN/11/6eme L of 22 January 2011, the Banque Centrale de Djibouti's board is made up of the Governor and six administrators appointed by decree, so every seat other than the Governor's is filled by the executive. The bank's own 2024 annual report states that composition, calls the board the bank's supreme organ and cites the 2011 law, which shows the arrangement still stands. This is a standing arrangement with no end date. The record rests on the bank's annual report, not on the text of the law, which could not be obtained.
events.quote: Il est compose du Gouverneur et de six administrateurs nommes par decret.

parties.role: appoints the central bank's six administrators by decree

events.summary: Decision 502/4 of the Monetary and Credit Council of the Central Bank of Syria, dated in Damascus on 10 May 2009, lowered the required cash reserve ratio on deposits funding industrial-sector lending. The decision is signed by the Council's chairman, Dr Adib Mayaleh, and its secretary, Layla Tanos, and carries below them the word certified and the signature of the Prime Minister, Mohammad Naji Otri, so the bank's own monetary decision went out over the head of government's approval. The decision is issued under Law 23 of 2002 on the Central Bank of Syria and the basic monetary system; the document does not say whether that law requires the Prime Minister's certification, and the text of the law itself could not be obtained.
events.source_title: Monetary and Credit Council Decision 502/4 of 10 May 2009 (Central Bank of Syria)
